arXiv:1812.02818v1 [nlin.PS] 19 Nov 2018

Anti-Chaos Control via Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations for the secured optical communication

Zhenyu Tang Email: zhenyutang2011@gmail.com    Hui-Ling Zhen
Abstract

Coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations, governing the propagation of envelopes of electromagnetic waves in birefringent optical fibers, are studied in this paper for their potential applications in the secured optical communication. Periodicity and integrability of the CNLS equations are obtained via the phase-plane analysis. With the time-delay and perturbations introduced, CNLS equations are chaotified and a chaotic system is proposed. Numerical and analytical methods are conducted on such system: (I) Phase projections are given and the final chaotic states can be observed. (II) Power spectra and the largest Lyapunov exponents are calculated to corroborate that those motions are indeed chaotic.


Keywords: Chaotification; Couple nonlinear Schrödinger equations; Chaotic Motion; Time delay

Interest in the optical solitons has grown for their potential applications in the telecommunications and ultrafast signal routing systems, especially the vector ones [1, 2]. The coupled nonlinear Schrödinger (CNLS) equations, which can be used to govern the propagation of envelopes of electromagnetic waves in birefringent optical fibers, read as [3, 4],

i​ux+ut​t+2​κ​(|u|2+|v|2)​u=0,\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912ptiu_{x}+u_{tt}+2\kappa(|u|^{2}+|v|^{2})u=0, (1)
i​vx+vt​t+2​κ​(|u|2+|v|2)​v=0,\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912ptiv_{x}+v_{tt}+2\kappa(|u|^{2}+|v|^{2})v=0, (2)

where uu and vv, two complex functions about xx and tt, are the normalized envelopes of the optical pulses along the two circularly polarized modes of a birefringent optical fiber, xx represents the normalized distance along the direction of propagation, tt refers to the retarded time, and κ\kappa gives the strength of the nonlinearity [3, 4]. Some studies on Eqs. (1) have been investigated in the early literatures, e.g., the bright soliton solutions [5], dark soliton solutions [6] and the effects of noise on the solitons [7].

Chaotic dynamics, owing to its noise-like broadband power spectra, is a good candidate to fight narrow-band effects, such as the frequency-selective fading or narrow-band disturbances in the communication systems [8, 9]. Thus, for the secured optical communication, chaotic signals have received increasing attention because of their dependence on the initial condition, which makes it difficult to guess the structure of the generator and to predict the signal over a longer time interval [10, 11]. Therefore, as opposed to controlling or eliminating chaos in dynamical systems [12], creating chaos from a non-chaotic system attracts some interests for the secured optical communication and information security [13]. People have known that a system with time-delay is inherently infinite dimensional, so it can produce complicated dynamics such as bifurcation and chaos, even a first-order system [15, 16]. So the time-delay feedback method has been thought as a straightforward one to chaotify a non-chaotic system [17].

Early literatures have investigated that the dark solitons array can be used in the secured optical communication [18, 19], and the results are claimed to benefit the study on soliton equations in such field [18]. However, to our knowledge, little work has been done on Eqs. (1) for their potential applications in the secured optical communication. In this paper, as an interest in chaos, analytical and numerical studies will be conducted on Eqs. (1) to reveal their potential applications in this field.

Setting u⁡(x,t)=φ⁡(ξ)​ei​ϑ1u(x,t)=\varphi(\xi)e^{i\vartheta_{1}}, v⁡(x,t)=ψ⁡(ξ)​ei​ϑ2v(x,t)=\psi(\xi)e^{i\vartheta_{2}} with ξ=a1​x−b1​t\xi=a_{1}x-b_{1}t, ϑ1=a2​x−b2​t\vartheta_{1}=a_{2}x-b_{2}t and ϑ2=a3​x−b3​t\vartheta_{2}=a_{3}x-b_{3}t, and substituting them into Eqs. (1), we have

φξ​ξ−o1​φ+o2​φ3+o2​ψ2​φ=0,\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pt\varphi_{\xi\xi}-o_{1}\varphi+o_{2}\varphi^{3}+o_{2}\psi^{2}\varphi=0, (3)
ψξ​ξ−o3​ψ+o4​ψ3+o4​φ2​ψ=0,\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pt\psi_{\xi\xi}-o_{3}\psi+o_{4}\psi^{3}+o_{4}\varphi^{2}\psi=0, (4)

where

o1=a2+b22b12,o2=2​κb12,o3=a3+b32b12,o4=2​κb12,\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pto_{1}=\frac{a_{2}+b_{2}^{2}}{b_{1}^{2}},\ \ o_{2}=\frac{2\kappa}{b_{1}^{2}},\ \ o_{3}=\frac{a_{3}+b_{3}^{2}}{b_{1}^{2}},\ \ o_{4}=\frac{2\kappa}{b_{1}^{2}},

with aja_{j}’s and bjb_{j}’s (j=1,2,3j=1,2,3) all being real constants.

To investigate the dynamical characteristics of Eqs. (1), we rewrite Eqs. (3) in the form of a four-dimensional planar dynamic system as follows (X1≡φX_{1}\equiv\varphi, X2≡ψX_{2}\equiv\psi, Y1≡φξY_{1}\equiv\varphi_{\xi}, Y2≡ψξY_{2}\equiv\psi_{\xi}):

{X1,ξ=Y1,X2,ξ=Y2,Y1,ξ=o1X1−o2X13−o2X22X1,Y2,ξ=o3X2−o4X23−o4X12X2.\hskip-48.36958pt\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}\vskip 4.2679ptX_{1,\xi}=Y_{1},\ \ \ X_{2,\xi}=Y_{2},\\ \vskip 4.2679ptY_{1,\xi}=o_{1}X_{1}-o_{2}X_{1}^{3}-o_{2}X_{2}^{2}X_{1},\ \ \ Y_{2,\xi}=o_{3}X_{2}-o_{4}X_{2}^{3}-o_{4}X_{1}^{2}X_{2}.\end{array}\right. (5)

Phase projections for System (5) are shown in Figs. 1, and power spectra for the solutions of System (5) are calculated in Figs. 2.

From Figs. 1, we can see the closed curves, which can be used to represent the phase projections of System (5). Based on the power spectra in Figs. 2, periodicity of Eqs. (1) is verified owing to the single frequency in Figs. 2. Thus, owing to the conclusions in Refs. [20, 21], we know that System (5) is integrable, and Eqs. (1) do not admit any chaotic motions. Hereby, f​f​t​(X1)fft(X_{1}) and f​f​t​(X2)fft(X_{2}) represent the fast Fourier transform (FFT) of X1X_{1} and X2X_{2}, respectively [14].

System (5) can be rewritten as

(X1X2Y1Y2)ξ=(Y1Y2o1​X1−o2​X13−o2​X22​X1o3​X2−o4​X23−o4​X12​X2),\displaystyle\left(\begin{array}[]{c}X_{1}\\ X_{2}\\ Y_{1}\\ Y_{2}\end{array}\right)_{\xi}=\left(\begin{array}[]{c}Y_{1}\\ Y_{2}\\ o_{1}X_{1}-o_{2}X_{1}^{3}-o_{2}X_{2}^{2}X_{1}\\ o_{3}X_{2}-o_{4}X_{2}^{3}-o_{4}X_{1}^{2}X_{2}\end{array}\right),

with 𝐱𝟏=(0,0,0,0)′\mathbf{x_{1}}=(0,0,0,0)^{{}^{\prime}}, 𝐱𝟐=(±o1o2,0,0,0)′\mathbf{x_{2}}=\left(\pm\sqrt{\frac{o_{1}}{o_{2}}},0,0,0\right)^{{}^{\prime}} and 𝐱𝟑=(0,±o3o4,0,0)′\mathbf{x_{3}}=\left(0,\pm\sqrt{\frac{o_{3}}{o_{4}}},0,0\right)^{{}^{\prime}} being its equilibrium points, where ′ denotes the vector transpose. Without loss of generality, we choose o1o_{1} and o3o_{3} as the control parameters.

According to the time-delay feedback method [13, 17], chaotifying System (5) is equivalent to to construct a single-input single-output system as follows:

{𝐱ξ=𝐟⁡(𝐱)+𝐠⁡(𝐱)​δ​(ξ),y=h⁡(𝐱),\hskip-48.36958pt\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}\vskip 4.2679pt\mathbf{x}_{\xi}=\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})+\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})\delta(\xi),\\ \vskip 4.2679pty=h(\mathbf{x}),\end{array}\right. (15)

where 𝐱\mathbf{x} and yy label the input and output, respectively, xξ=d​x/d​ξ\textbf{x}_{\xi}=d\textbf{x}/d\xi, 𝐟⁡(𝐱)\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}) and 𝐠⁡(𝐱)\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}) are both real vector functions, δ⁡(ξ)\delta(\xi) corresponds to a system parameter perturbation or an exogenous control input, and h⁡(𝐱)h(\mathbf{x}) is a smooth real function and refers to the output [13, 17]. Hereby, in the case of System (Anti-Chaos Control via Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations for the secured optical communication), 𝐱=(X1,X2,Y1,Y2)′\mathbf{x}=(X_{1},X_{2},Y_{1},Y_{2})^{{}^{\prime}}, while 𝐟⁡(𝐱)\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}) and 𝐠⁡(𝐱)\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}) can be given as

𝐟⁡(𝐱)=(Y1Y2o1​X1−o2​X13−o2​X22​X1o3​X2−o4​X23−o4​X12​X2),𝐠⁡(𝐱)=(00X1X2).\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pt\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})=\left(\begin{array}[]{c}Y_{1}\\ Y_{2}\\ o_{1}X_{1}-o_{2}X_{1}^{3}-o_{2}X_{2}^{2}X_{1}\\ o_{3}X_{2}-o_{4}X_{2}^{3}-o_{4}X_{1}^{2}X_{2}\end{array}\right),\ \ \ \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})=\left(\begin{array}[]{c}0\\ 0\\ X_{1}\\ X_{2}\end{array}\right).

Then, System (15) can be embodied as

{𝐱ξ=(Y1Y2o1​X1−o2​X13−o2​X22​X1o3​X2−o4​X23−o4​X12​X2)+(00X1X2)​δ​(ξ),y=h⁡(𝐱),\hskip-48.36958pt\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}\vskip 4.2679pt\mathbf{x}_{\xi}=\left(\begin{array}[]{c}Y_{1}\\ Y_{2}\\ o_{1}X_{1}-o_{2}X_{1}^{3}-o_{2}X_{2}^{2}X_{1}\\ o_{3}X_{2}-o_{4}X_{2}^{3}-o_{4}X_{1}^{2}X_{2}\end{array}\right)+\left(\begin{array}[]{c}0\\ 0\\ X_{1}\\ X_{2}\end{array}\right)\delta(\xi),\\ \vskip 4.2679pty=h(\mathbf{x}),\end{array}\right. (25)

where h⁡(𝐱)h(\mathbf{x}) and δ⁡(ξ)\delta(\xi) are to be determined.

Based on Expression (Anti-Chaos Control via Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations for the secured optical communication), we have

𝐚𝐝𝐟​𝐠​(𝐱)=(−X1−X2Y1Y2),𝐚𝐝𝐟2​𝐠​(𝐱)=(−2​Y1−2​Y22​o1​X1−4​o2​X13+(2​o1−2​o2)​X1​X222​o3​X2−4​o4​X23+(2​o3−2​o4)​X2​X12),\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pt\mathbf{ad_{f}g}(\mathbf{x})=\left(\begin{array}[]{c}-X_{1}\\ -X_{2}\\ Y_{1}\\ Y_{2}\end{array}\right),\ \ \ \mathbf{ad_{f}}^{2}\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})=\left(\begin{array}[]{c}-2Y_{1}\\ -2Y_{2}\\ 2o_{1}X_{1}-4o_{2}X_{1}^{3}+(2o_{1}-2o_{2})X_{1}X_{2}^{2}\\ 2o_{3}X_{2}-4o_{4}X_{2}^{3}+(2o_{3}-2o_{4})X_{2}X_{1}^{2}\end{array}\right),
𝐚𝐝𝐟3​𝐠​(𝐱)=(−4​o1​X1+6​o2​X13+(4​o2−2​o1)​X1​X22−4​o3​Xx+6​o4​X23+(4​o4−2​o3)​X2​X12Y1​[4​o1−18​o2​X12+(2​o1−4​o2)​X22]+(4​o1−8​o2)​X1​X2​Y2Y1​[4​o3−18​o4​X22+(2​o3−4​o4)​X12]+(4​o3−8​o4)​X1​X2​Y1),\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pt\mathbf{ad_{f}}^{3}\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})=\left(\begin{array}[]{c}-4o_{1}X_{1}+6o_{2}X_{1}^{3}+(4o_{2}-2o_{1})X_{1}X_{2}^{2}\\ -4o_{3}X_{x}+6o_{4}X_{2}^{3}+(4o_{4}-2o_{3})X_{2}X_{1}^{2}\\ Y_{1}[4o_{1}-18o_{2}X_{1}^{2}+(2o_{1}-4o_{2})X_{2}^{2}]+(4o_{1}-8o_{2})X_{1}X_{2}Y_{2}\\ Y_{1}[4o_{3}-18o_{4}X_{2}^{2}+(2o_{3}-4o_{4})X_{1}^{2}]+(4o_{3}-8o_{4})X_{1}X_{2}Y_{1}\end{array}\right),

where adf​g​(x)\textbf{ad}_{\textbf{f}}\textbf{g}(\textbf{x}) refers to the Lie bracket [13, 17] of the two smooth vector functions 𝐟⁡(𝐱)\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}) and 𝐠⁡(𝐱)\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}). Note that the relative degree of System (25) is four, i.e., the dimension of 𝐱\mathbf{x}, and the definition of “relative degree” can be seen in Refs. [13, 17].

Via the conclusions in Refs. [13, 17], h⁡(𝐱)h(\mathbf{x}) should satisfy

∂h⁡(𝐱)∂𝐱​[𝐠⁡(𝐱),𝐚𝐝𝐟​𝐠​(𝐱),𝐚𝐝𝐟2​𝐠​(𝐱)]=0.\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pt\frac{\partial h(\mathbf{x})}{\partial\mathbf{x}}[\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{ad_{f}g}(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{ad_{f}}^{2}\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})]=0.

Based on some calculations, it means that h⁡(𝐱)h(\mathbf{x}) can be expressed as

h⁡(𝐱)=X2​Y1−X1​Y2,\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pth(\mathbf{x})=X_{2}Y_{1}-X_{1}Y_{2}, (40)

which gives rise to the expressions of δ⁡(ξ)\delta(\xi) as follows:

δ⁡(ξ)=ς​sin⁡[σ⁡(X2​(ξ−τ)​Y1​(ξ−τ)−X1​(ξ−τ)​Y2​(ξ−τ))],\displaystyle\hskip-42.67912pt\delta(\xi)=\varsigma\sin[\sigma(X_{2}(\xi-\tau)Y_{1}(\xi-\tau)-X_{1}(\xi-\tau)Y_{2}(\xi-\tau))], (41)

where ς\varsigma and σ\sigma are both the real constants, τ\tau refers to the time-delay, and ξ\xi is given in Sec. 2.

Therefore, based on the chaotification of Eqs. (1), we can propose a chaotic system as follows:

(X1X2Y1Y2)ξ=(Y1Y2(o1+δ)​X1−o2​X13−o2​X22​X1(o3+δ)​X2−o4​X23−o4​X12​X2),\displaystyle\left(\begin{array}[]{c}X_{1}\\ X_{2}\\ Y_{1}\\ Y_{2}\end{array}\right)_{\xi}=\left(\begin{array}[]{c}Y_{1}\\ Y_{2}\\ (o_{1}+\delta)X_{1}-o_{2}X_{1}^{3}-o_{2}X_{2}^{2}X_{1}\\ (o_{3}+\delta)X_{2}-o_{4}X_{2}^{3}-o_{4}X_{1}^{2}X_{2}\end{array}\right),

where δ=δ⁡(ξ)=ς​sin⁡[σ⁡(X2​(ξ−τ)​Y1​(ξ−τ)−X1​(ξ−τ)​Y2​(ξ−τ))]\delta=\delta(\xi)=\varsigma\sin[\sigma(X_{2}(\xi-\tau)Y_{1}(\xi-\tau)-X_{1}(\xi-\tau)Y_{2}(\xi-\tau))] can be used as the perturbations of the control parameters o1o_{1} and o3o_{3}.

To study the final chaotic states of System (Anti-Chaos Control via Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations for the secured optical communication), we investigate the phase projections of Y1Y_{1} and Y2Y_{2} in Figs. 3(a) and 4(a), respectively, and calculate their respective power spectra in Figs. 3(b) and 4(b). Comparing Figs. 3(b) with 2(a), 4(b) with 2(b), respectively, we can see that the original frequencies have been both broken, and chaotic motions occur. Note that the solutions of System (Anti-Chaos Control via Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations for the secured optical communication) ignore the driver periods and represent a random sequence of uncorrelated shocks, so those chaotic motions are the “developed” ones [24, 25].

In this paper, we have discussed the CNLS equations [i.e., Eqs. (1)], which describe the propagation of envelopes of electromagnetic waves in birefringent optical fibers, for their potential applications in the secured optical communication. With the time-delay and perturbations introduced into Eqs. (1), we have constructed a chaotic system and its final chaotic motions, with the phase projections and power spectra given. Further, soliton solutions and soliton propagation of such chaotic system have been studied when time-delay is fixed. As a generalization, the main results of this paper can be summarized as follows:

∙\bullet Reducing Eqs. (1) into the equivalent four-dimensional planar dynamic system [i.e., System (5)], we have obtained the integrability and periodicity of Eqs. (1) from the phase projections and power spectra, as displayed in Figs. 1-2.

∙\bullet With time-delay and perturbations into System (5), we have chaotified Eqs. (1) and a chaotic system [i.e., System Anti-Chaos Control via Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations for the secured optical communication] has been constructed.

∙\bullet Chaotic motions of System (Anti-Chaos Control via Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations for the secured optical communication) have been displayed via the phase projections, as shown in Figs. 3(a) and 4(a), and the respective power spectra have been calculated in Figs.3(b) and 4(b).
